source.citation: Spycher, N., Pruess, K., Ennis-King, J. (2003). CO2-H2O mixtures in the geological sequestration of CO2. I. Assessment and calculation of mutual solubilities from 12 to 100 C and up to 600 bar. Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta 67(16), 3015-3031.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF from the publisher), Section 2.1, p. 3016, read on its text layer
transcription.note: The values are those the authors quote for pure carbon dioxide, from Span and Wagner (1996) and Angus et al. (1976), and for the three-phase coexistence of the CO2-H2O system, from Wendland et al. (1999); they are reference points of the pure fluid, not measurements of the article.

co2_critical_temperature_C.description: Critical temperature of pure carbon dioxide in degrees Celsius, from Span and Wagner (1996).

co2_critical_pressure.description: Critical pressure of pure carbon dioxide, from Span and Wagner (1996).

co2_vapor_pressure_25C.description: Vapor pressure of pure carbon dioxide at 298.15 K, from Span and Wagner (1996); the article gives 64.32 bar from the data of Angus et al. (1976) beside it.

three_phase_pressure_25C.description: Pressure of the three-phase coexistence (water-rich liquid, carbon dioxide-rich liquid, vapor) of the CO2-H2O system at 298.15 K, from Wendland et al. (1999).
